Migrating from jose

Source: vignettes/articles/migrating-from-jose.Rmd
migrating-from-jose.Rmd

The CRAN package jose reads and writes JWKs and encodes and decodes JWTs on top of OpenSSL. This article maps its functions to zujose’s and explains what changes. zujose does not mirror jose’s API: the differences below are the point of the move, and a compatibility layer would hide them.

library(zujose)

Function by function

jose 2.0 zujose
jwt_claim(iss, sub, aud, exp, ...) a plain named list; expires_in and not_before in jose_jwt_encode() set exp and nbf
jwt_encode_hmac(claim, secret, size = 256) jose_jwt_encode(claims, jose_key_oct(secret), alg = "HS256")
jwt_decode_hmac(jwt, secret) jose_jwt_decode(jwt, jose_key_oct(secret), algorithms = "HS256")
jwt_encode_sig(claim, key, size = 256) jose_jwt_encode(claims, as_jose_key(pem), alg = "RS256"), or "ES256", "PS256"…
jwt_decode_sig(jwt, pubkey) jose_jwt_decode(jwt, as_jose_key(pem), algorithms = "RS256")
jwt_split(jwt) jose_peek(jwt)
jwk_read(x), read_jwk(x) as_jose_key(x), or as_jose_keyset(x) for a JWK Set
jwk_write(x), write_jwk(x) jose_jwk(x); jose_pem(x) for PEM
base64url_encode(x), base64url_decode(x) zuutf::base64_encode(x, url = TRUE, pad = FALSE), zuutf::base64_decode(x, url = TRUE)

zujose also covers what jose does not: JWE, the JSON serializations, detached and unencoded payloads (RFC 7797), key sets, thumbprints, and encrypted JWTs.

What changes

You name the algorithms

jwt_decode_hmac() and jwt_decode_sig() take the algorithm from the token’s header, limited only by the type of key. jose_jwt_decode() has an algorithms argument with no default, and refuses any other algorithm before it does any cryptography. This closes algorithm confusion, where a token picks a weaker algorithm than the one you meant (RFC 8725, section 2.1).

Claims are checked, and exp is required

jose checks exp and nbf when a token has them. zujose checks them too, with the same 60 second leeway, and also:

  • requires exp by default (required = "exp"), so a token that never expires is refused unless you set required = character();
  • checks iat is not in the future, and max_age when you give one;
  • matches aud, iss and sub against audience, issuer and subject, and any claim against claims.

Keys are typed

jose takes a secret as a string or raw vector and a public key as an openssl key object. zujose takes a jose_key built from raw bytes, JWK text or PEM. A string is not taken as a secret, because a password is not a key:

secret <- charToRaw("a shared secret of at least 32 bytes!")
key <- jose_key_oct(secret)

A key may name its one algorithm with alg, and is then refused for any other.

Errors have classes

jose signals errors with stop() and a message. zujose raises conditions classed by cause, such as zujose_expired_error or zujose_audience_error, all inheriting from zujose_error. Catch the class, not the text; ?zujose_error lists them.

A worked example

A service that used jose to issue and check HMAC tokens:

library(jose)
secret <- charToRaw("a shared secret of at least 32 bytes!")
jwt <- jwt_encode_hmac(
  jwt_claim(sub = "user-17", aud = "orders-api", exp = Sys.time() + 600),
  secret = secret
)
claims <- jwt_decode_hmac(jwt, secret = secret)
stopifnot(claims$aud == "orders-api")

does the same with zujose like this:

key <- jose_key_oct(secret, alg = "HS256")
jwt <- jose_jwt_encode(
  list(sub = "user-17", aud = "orders-api"),
  key,
  expires_in = 600
)
claims <- jose_jwt_decode(jwt, key, algorithms = "HS256", audience = "orders-api")
claims$sub
#> [1] "user-17"

The audience check moves into the decode call, where it cannot be forgotten.

Both packages write standard JWTs, so tokens already issued keep working after the move, with one exception: a token without exp is refused unless you change required. zujose’s tests check its JWTs against tokens made by PyJWT, an independent implementation, for every signature algorithm.

To verify tokens from an OpenID Connect provider, read its JWK Set into a key set; Verifying tokens against a JWKS shows how to fetch and cache it.
